walkthroughs.body_html:
A force is just a push or a pull.

You feel forces every day — kicking a ball, opening a door, even sitting on a chair. Forces can be contact (like friction) or non-contact (like gravity).

We measure forces in newtons (N). One newton is roughly the weight of a small apple. 🍎

Mass is how much stuff is in an object. It's in kilograms (kg) and never changes.

Weight is the pull of gravity on that mass. It's a force, so it's in newtons (N).

On Earth, gravity pulls with about g = 10 N/kg. So a 1 kg bag of sugar weighs about 10 N.

When more than one force acts on an object, we add them up to get the resultant force.

If you push a box right with 8 N and friction pulls left with 3 N, the resultant is 5 N to the right.

If the resultant is zero, the object is balanced — it stays still or keeps moving at the same speed.
